full_judgment:
The predecessor-in-interest of the opposite parties, Abdul Hashim instituted Misc. Case No. 134 of 1970 against the petitioner and others in the 4th Court of Munsif (now Assistant Judge), Habiganj for pre-emption of the case land under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, claiming to be a co-sharer by purchase of the case land from the opposite parties No. 2-5 of the said Misc. Case, by a kabala dated 29-6-1970 at a consideration of Taka 3000.00. The pre-emptor Abdul Hasim also purchased some land out of the said holding by kabala dated 4th June, 1970 from Shoajan Bibi who is a co-sharer of the said opposite parties 2-5 and as such the pre-emptor Abdul Hashim is a co-sharer of the said holding by purchase. The petitioner is a stranger purchaser and as such the pre-emptor is entitled to pre-empt the case land. 

 4. The petitioner along with others contested the said case by filing a separate written Objection and prayed for pre-emption of the case land under section 96(4) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as co-sharers by inheritance. In their written objection also it was specifically stated that the case is bad for defect of parties since Ebad Ullah, Afaiot Ullah, Rois Ullah, Meher Ullah, Jalima Bibi, Maremchand Bibi, Ramid Ullah, Majjob Ullah, Najabat Bibi and heirs of Abul Hossain and Ajmot Ullah who are co-sharers of the said holding were left out. As they appeared in time and prayed for pre-emption in time, their prayer for pre-emption may be allowed on receipt of the price of land transferred along with interest thereon. 

 21. Mr. Jyotirmoy Narayan Deb, the learned Advocate for the opposite party Nos.l and 2, in support of his contentions has placed the case of Ramjeewean vs. Chand Mohammad, reported in AIR 1976 (Rajasthan) 65 and submitted that in an appropriate case the court has power to bring the heirs of the respondents on record but for that an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act is required to be filed by the party concerned explaining the cause of delay but in the instant case that has not been done. He also cited the case of Muhammad Jamal vs. Chairman, Industrial Court reported in 16 DLR (SC) 386 but in course of his submission he states that the facts of that case are distinguishable from the present case. 

 22. Thus from our above discussion it is clear that the heirs of deceased respondent No. 1 Abdul Hashim were brought on record within time in the original Misc. Case in the trial Court but at the time of preparation of the memo of appeal the deceased respondent Abdul Hashim was made respondent instead of his heirs who were already brought on record in the Misc. case in the trial Court within time. It is submitted that this was due to bonafide mistake of the learned Advocate for which the client should not suffer. It is also submitted that the mistake of the learned Advocate in not adding the heirs of the deceased respondent is due to the fact that in the judgment of the trial Court deceased Abdul Hashim was shown as the petitioner and this has led to the bonafide mistake of the learned Advocate for which the client should not suffer. It is also submitted that in the application under section 153 CPC filed before the court of Subordinate Judge, Habiganj in Misc. Appeal No. 166 of 1982 for striking out the name of Abdul Hashim and for bringing the legal heirs of respondent Abdul Hashim in the memorandum of appeal who were already on record it was stated that the respondent Abdul Hashim died during pendency of the original Misc. case and his heirs were duly substituted in the trial Court but at the time of preferring appeal the heirs of deceased Abdul Hashim were not impleaded as respondents in his place and deceased Abdul Hashim was made respondent and this was done due to mistake of the learned Advocate which is required to be corrected. Thus it is apparent that there was no laches on the part of the party concerned and the mistake was due to the bonafide omission of the learned Advocate. It is not disputed that the heirs of deceased respondent Abdul Hashim were brought on record in the trial Court within time. In the instant case in the memo of appeal the name of deceased respondent Abdul Hashim was mentioned through inadvertence but his heirs were already on record in the original proceeding. As the heirs of deceased respondent were already on record within time in the original proceeding even if the appeal has abated the court has power to allow the amendment and add the legal representatives of the deceased. The fact that a dead man had been made party by mistake does not deprive the court of the power to implead his legal representatives under section 153 CPC.
